READING

**The grant arithmetic: the critical flaw in PENDLARROW**

The 31.8 per cent figure is calculated as (£504,000 + £118,000) / (£1,840,000 + £118,000), which uses year-to-2026-03-31 small animal revenue of £1,336,000 as the denominator's small animal component, then adds Ardgowrie on top. The assessment happens on 2027-04-30, thirteen months later. Small animal has grown at eleven per cent a year for four consecutive years. The most reasonable reading of "annualised value of work in force on that date" is the current run rate at that date, annualised.

Work through the threshold:

- Small animal in force at April 2027, annualised: £1,336,000 × 1.11^(13/12) ≈ £1,496,000 (rounding generously)
- Farm/equine in force, annualised (Ardgowrie plus existing): £622,000 (flat)
- Total: £2,118,000
- Ratio: £622,000 / £2,118,000 = **29.3 per cent**

For the thirty per cent threshold to hold with farm/equine fixed at £622,000, total turnover cannot exceed £2,073,333, which means small animal cannot exceed £1,451,333. The year-to-March-2027 small animal figure (one clean year at eleven per cent) is £1,336,000 × 1.11 = £1,482,960. The overshoot is about £31,600 — roughly 2.4 per cent of the small animal base. For PENDLARROW to qualify, small animal growth in the year to March 2027 would need to be below 8.6 per cent. That is materially below a four-year consistent trend, and the Ordsall Green surgery, when it opens, will push small animal volumes further up, not down.

If instead the assessor uses trailing twelve months to April 2027 (May 2026 to April 2027):

- Farm/equine trailing twelve months: existing £504,000 plus six months of Ardgowrie (£59,000) = £563,000
- Small animal trailing twelve months: approximately £1,482,000 to £1,496,000
- Ratio: around 27.4 per cent

Under no consistent methodology that reflects the actual state of the practice at April 2027 does farm/equine reach thirty per cent. The 31.8 per cent figure only works if the assessor takes the prior year's small animal revenue while simultaneously projecting Ardgowrie forward — mixing time periods in a way that favours the applicant. A formal grant assessor will not do that.

**The grant was the entire financial case for PENDLARROW**

Strip out the £100,000 grant and the Ardgowrie contract stands on its own:

- Revenue: £118,000
- Dedicated farm vet (including on-costs): £71,000
- Fitted vehicle (capital): £34,000
- Gross annual margin after vet pay: £47,000
- Vehicle recovered over, say, five years: roughly £6,800/year equivalent

That is a contribution of approximately £40,000 per year before: any overhead allocation to the farm division, the cost of building and staffing a night-call rota, drug and equipment inventory for 900 dairy cattle, vehicle running costs, and management time. Fully loaded, the margin is thin at best and may be negative.

For that £47,000 gross margin the practice must:

- Hire one dedicated vet immediately
- Spend £34,000 on a vehicle immediately, reducing the deposit to £16,000 after the fit-out (£310,000 − £260,000 − £34,000 = £16,000, which is a very narrow cash position for a practice of this size with no borrowing facility)
- Take on the night rota that the outgoing practice surrendered after nine years for precisely this reason
- Commit to holding at least 700 cattle under herd health contract until 2030-04-30 — meaning Ardgowrie cannot be exited cleanly even if night calls prove unsustainable

Compare WESTERGATE: cash after fit-out is £50,000, next hire goes into small animal, no night rota, no 2030 obligation.

**The night-call signal**

The prior practice gave up Ardgowrie after nine years specifically because of the night call-out load. That is not a negotiating position or a gripe; it is the reason stated on a handover call, after nearly a decade of working the contract. Kirstie Ballantyne-Rowe moving with it is helpful — she knows the herd and the farm — but she cannot carry all night calls alone. Staffing a farm out-of-hours rota in addition to the existing Marchwold hills work is not a footnote; it is the operational problem that ended the previous relationship.

**The 2030 lock-in and repayment risk**

If — contrary to the arithmetic above — the grant were awarded, the practice would need to hold a ≥700-cattle herd health contract through 2030-04-30. Ardgowrie is 900 cattle today, so the contract satisfies the threshold; but the termination risk runs both ways. If Ardgowrie leaves, or reduces to fewer than 700 cattle under the contract's scope, £100,000 becomes repayable in full. A contract that one practice surrendered and that the practice is being asked to pick up in its place carries exactly the kind of continuity risk that makes this exposure real.

**Strategic direction**

Small animal is growing at eleven per cent per year; it has done so for four consecutive years; the Ordsall Green surgery is a small animal surgery. Farm/equine is flat for three years and there is nothing in the brief suggesting that changes. Under PENDLARROW, the next hire serves a stagnant segment with a thin margin and a night burden. Under WESTERGATE, the next hire goes into the segment that has compounded at eleven per cent, directly supporting the new surgery.

The farm/equine share of turnover is going to decline regardless: the numerator is approximately flat and the denominator grows at eleven per cent on the small animal portion. Even with Ardgowrie, the share is sub-thirty per cent by the assessment date. There is no strategic commitment here that changes the long-run direction of the business; there is only a medium-term lock-in at a high operational cost.

**Summary comparison**

| | PENDLARROW | WESTERGATE |
|---|---|---|
| Cash after fit-out + vehicle | £16,000 | £50,000 |
| Grant received | £0 (threshold fails) | £0 |
| Annual gross margin from Ardgowrie | ~£47,000 before overhead and night rota | — |
| Night-call obligation | Yes, to 2030 minimum | No |
| Repayment exposure | £100,000 if cattle threshold breached | None |
| Next hire | Farm vet (flat segment) | Small animal (growing at 11%) |
| Strategic alignment | Against growth trend | With growth trend |

The arithmetic removes the grant. Without the grant, PENDLARROW is a thin-margin farm contract with a heavy operational burden, a tight immediate cash position, and a multi-year lock-in — entered at a moment when the practice is already managing the significant project of fitting out and opening a second surgery.

WESTERGATE is simpler, safer, and directionally right. The hundred thousand pounds the PENDLARROW summary claims to be forgoing is most probably not on the table under either course.

READING
The grant that is the entire material case for PENDLARROW is examined against the assessment methodology stated in the brief. "Annualised value of the work in force on 2027-04-30" applied to a practice where small animal has grown eleven per cent for four consecutive years produces an annualised small animal figure of approximately £1,496,000 at that date, against which farm and equine at £622,000 gives a ratio of about 29.3 per cent — below the thirty-per-cent threshold under any consistent methodology. The threshold only clears 30 per cent if the assessor uses the year-to-2026-03-31 small animal revenue while simultaneously projecting Ardgowrie forward; no grant body will apply that cross-period mix. For the threshold to be met the practice would need small animal growth to fall below 8.6 per cent, materially below a four-year trend that the new Ordsall Green surgery will accelerate rather than slow. Strip the £100,000 away and what remains under PENDLARROW is: a £47,000 gross annual margin (before overhead, before night-rota staffing, before vehicle running costs) against a dedicated hire, a £34,000 vehicle spend that reduces immediately available cash to £16,000, the night-call burden that ended a nine-year relationship between Ardgowrie and the outgoing practice, a commitment to hold ≥700 cattle through 2030-04-30 under repayment risk, and a strategic lock-in to a segment that has been flat for three years while small animal compounds at eleven per cent. WESTERGATE costs £260,000 from deposit, leaves £50,000 available, puts the next hire into the growing segment, and carries none of those obligations. Because the grant is the sole financial justification for PENDLARROW and it almost certainly does not materialise, the two courses are not forgoing £100,000 versus keeping it; they are roughly equal on grant outcome and unequal on everything else.

CALL
WESTERGATE

GROUNDS
The thirty-per-cent threshold will not be met at the April 2027 assessment because one further year of eleven-per-cent small animal growth raises the annualised total past the level at which farm-and-equine can remain thirty per cent of it, so PENDLARROW most likely forfeits the same hundred thousand pounds as WESTERGATE while also acquiring the night-call burden the outgoing practice surrendered, a multi-year lock-in, a thinly margined contract, and an immediate cash position of sixteen thousand pounds.
